description: LFO x EG: the Surge XT modulator, an LFO with eight shapes including two random modes and a step sequencer, scaled by a six-stage envelope

params.text: Sets the rate of the LFO, and can be tempo-synced; in step sequencer mode one cycle covers the whole sequence.
Sets the phase the LFO starts from; in step sequencer mode it shuffles the step timing.
Bends the shape of the wave, and does something different for each shape; the menu offers further deform types for several of them.
Scales the height of the LFO wave.
Holds the envelope at zero for this long after the gate arrives.
Sets how long the envelope takes to climb to full.
Holds the envelope at full for this long before the decay starts.
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall from full to the sustain level.
Sets the level the envelope holds at while the gate stays high.
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall to zero once the gate falls.
Chooses the LFO shape, from sine through the two random modes to the envelope and the step sequencer.
Switches the outputs from bipolar to unipolar: the wave runs 0V to 10V rather than 5V either way.
Modulation depth for one of the four modulation inputs into the knob it belongs to; the figure is the shift a plus or minus 10V signal produces.
Sets which trigger output that step fires: neither, A, B, or both.
Sets the first step the sequence loops from.
Sets the last step the sequence loops to.

inputs.text: A gate opens the envelope and resets the phase of the LFO.
A gate opens the envelope without resetting the phase of the LFO.
Sets the tempo for the tempo-synced controls, taking a quarter-note trigger or, when the menu is switched to BPM CV, a tempo voltage.
A 0-10V signal here stops the LFO cycling and sets its position in the wave directly.
Carries a modulation signal; arm it with its button, then turn a knob to set how far this signal moves that knob.

outputs.text: Carries the LFO wave scaled by the envelope.
Carries the LFO wave on its own, 5V either way, or 0-10V in unipolar mode.
Carries the envelope on its own, 0-5V, or 0-10V in unipolar mode.
A trigger at the end of each complete cycle of the wave.
A trigger at the end of each stage of the envelope, or at the steps marked A in the sequence.
A trigger at the end of the whole envelope, after the release, or at the steps marked B in the sequence.

notes: Drag across the step levels in the display to set them, double-click a step to reset it, and right-click one for a typing box and a list of presets that fill every step at once.
A modulation input does nothing until you press the button above it to arm it and then drag a knob; the drag sets how far that input moves that knob, and a ring on the knob shows the amount.
menu: Deform Type 1 — the first of the extra deform behaviours offered for the chosen shape; the number of them changes with the shape, and shapes with only one offer none.
Polyphony — a submenu carrying Trigger Sets Polyphony If Connected, No Trig or Trig Chan 1 Triggers All, and a channel count from 1 to 16.
Envelope Triggers from Zero — restarts the envelope from zero rather than from the level it had reached.
Envelope Smoothing — a submenu setting how much the envelope output is smoothed: None, Low, Medium or High; it is greyed out while Envelope Triggers from Zero is on.
Random Phase on Attack — starts the LFO at a random phase each time it is triggered.
Scale LFO and EG Outputs by Amp — applies the AMP knob to the separate LFO and EG outputs as well as to the combined one.
Set EG Output to Zero if Gate Absent — holds the EG output at zero while nothing is patched to the gate input.
Rack Randomization Changes Shape — allows Rack's randomise gesture to change the LFO shape.
Clock in QuarterNotes — reads the clock input as a quarter-note trigger, and the panel labels that jack CLOCK.
Clock in BPM CV — reads the clock input as a tempo voltage, and the panel labels that jack BPM.
Temposync LFO Rate — locks the LFO rate to the clock, in note divisions.
Temposync Env Rates — locks the envelope stage times to the clock, in note divisions.
Use Global Style — ties this module's appearance to the setting shared by every Surge XT module, rather than to this module alone.
Skin — sets the panel colouring: Dark, Medium or Light.
Colors — a submenu setting the colour of the Display Area, Knob and Slider Values, Modulations and Power Buttons, and carrying Show Knob Shadows.
Value Displays — a submenu carrying Knob Value Rings, Knob Modulation Animations and Display Modulation Animations.
